Subject: Jules Martin — final interview wrap + comp expectation

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for slotting time for Jules yesterday. Quick recap from my side: Jules is currently at FluxScale where they lead a small inference infra team; strengths were system-level debugging, latency regression investigations, and shipping a recent KV cache optimization. Interviewers liked the depth and the product judgment.

On compensation, Jules said target base is $210k with total comp target around $280k (base + equity + bonus). They noted flexibility on structure but are aiming for a move that matches level and scope (senior IC, leading cross-team infra projects).

Attached: resume (pdf). Candidate is ready for an offer conversation next week. Want to confirm internal band and whether we should propose at the top of band or request an exception.

Next steps suggested:
- Irene: hiring manager recommendation on level and target comp
- Marissa / Lauren: confirm band and exception path if required
- If approved, Lily will coordinate a call between Jules and our recruiter to review details.

Thanks,
Lily
Lily Tan | Senior Recruiter, RecruitCo
Cell: +1 415-555-0123

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Jules Martin — final interview wrap + comp expectation

Marissa / Lauren,

Thanks — quick debrief from interviews: consensus is Sr. Serving Engineer (IC3) with scope to own low-latency serving projects and mentor two engineers. Key wins: production debugging, shipped latency wins, strong cross-team influence. Risks: limited direct people management experience, but that's not required.

My recommendation: extend IC3 at a competitive package given scarcity of inference infra hires. I propose:
- Base: $230,000
- Equity: 0.30% 4y with 1y cliff
- Target bonus: 10%

This is slightly above the published IC3 midline; I think $230k puts us in a good position to close without breaking internal alignment. If we need to go to $240k I'd request a comp exception. I've attached a draft offer template with the numbers filled for your convenience.

Please advise on whether this sits in band or requires exception routing. If we can get signoff by Tue 14 Jul, Lily can schedule the offer call for Wed/Thu.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Hiring Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Jules Martin — final interview wrap + comp expectation

Irene — thanks for the write-up and the filled template. Band guidance:
- IC3 published base band: $180,000 - $220,000
- Pay philosophy: we generally make offers at or slightly above midpoint for strong candidates; anything above band high (>$220k) requires a level confirmation or an exception (comp committee).

Given the candidate profile and market constraints, we can approve up to $230,000 base within an elevated offer authorization (manager + DPE signoff). Anything >$230,000 needs VP-level exception and documented business case.

If you want to target $230k we can do a fast-track internal approval today (Irene approve + Vivek ack + HR admin). For $240k I need to route to exec comp committee (longer lead time).

Also flagging total comp modeling: equity pool and expected refresh cadence — Marissa, please confirm equity budget for this hire if we go to the top.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Total Rewards
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Jules Martin — final interview wrap + comp expectation

Folks — I reviewed the interview notes and the recommended impact. Jules looks like a rare infra hire and the hiring timeline is a factor. I'm comfortable signing off on $235,000 base with the following conditions:
- Provide a short business case (one paragraph) in the candidate file: why $235k vs $230k (recruiting difficulty, counteroffer risk, immediate impact areas)
- Commit to a 6-month check-in tied to delivery milestones (KV cache rollout and one cross-team latency project)

I want to avoid the exec comp committee route if possible; $235k is a reasonable middle ground and preserves speed. If Irene confirms the business case, Marissa can draft the final offer language.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Serving & Runtime
Redwood Inference
